papers.title: Thermo-Structural Simulation and Integrated Optimization of LPBF-Fabricated Inconel 718 Components: Effects of Part Orientation and Base Plate Material on Distortion, Residual Stress, and Temperature Distribution
papers.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) is widely employed for manufacturing complex metallic components; however, process-induced distortion, residual stress, and thermal accumulation remain major challenges affecting dimensional accuracy and structural integrity. In the present study, a three-dimensional thermo-structural finite element model was developed to investigate the combined influence of component orientation and base plate material on the thermo-mechanical behavior of LPBF-fabricated Inconel 718 components. In addition, an integrated optimization methodology combining response normalization, a weighted sum performance index, and radar chart analysis was adopted to realize the optimal combination of the process variables by a simultaneous consideration of distortion, residual stress, and temperature. Accordingly, five part orientations and five different base plate materials were examined under identical processing conditions through 25 simulation cases. The obtained results revealed that component orientation represents the dominant factor controlling distortion and residual stress development, whereas both orientation and base plate material significantly affect component temperature. The inclined orientations generated the highest distortion levels, while the vertical configuration exhibited the highest residual stresses. In contrast, the horizontal orientation along the X-direction demonstrated the most balanced thermo-mechanical performance. Furthermore, AlSi10Mg base plate material provided the lowest thermal accumulation due to its high thermal conductivity. The integrated optimization analysis based on radar chart assessment and performance index evaluation identified the Horizontal-X/Ti-6Al-4V and Horizontal-X/AlSi10Mg configurations as the most favorable LPBF conditions. These findings provide practical guidelines for selecting build orientation and base plate material to reduce thermo-mechanical defects, thereby improving the dimensional accuracy and manufacturing reliability of LPBF-fabricated Inconel 718 components.

summary_zh.motivation: LPBF制造Inconel 718部件时变形和残余应力问题突出，需优化工艺参数。
summary_zh.method: 建立三维热-结构有限元模型，结合响应归一化、加权性能指标和雷达图分析进行多目标优化。
summary_zh.result: 部件取向是控制变形和残余应力的主导因素，水平X方向性能最均衡，AlSi10Mg基板热积累最低。
summary_zh.validation: 通过25个仿真案例对比验证模型和优化方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: Process-induced distortion and residual stress in LPBF-fabricated Inconel 718 components degrade dimensional accuracy, necessitating optimization of build orientation and base plate material.
summary_en.method: A 3D thermo-structural finite element model was developed, combined with response normalization, weighted sum performance index, and radar chart analysis for multi-objective optimization.
summary_en.result: Part orientation dominated distortion and residual stress; horizontal-X orientation offered the best trade-off, while AlSi10Mg base plate minimized thermal accumulation.
summary_en.validation: The model and optimization methodology were validated through 25 simulation cases covering five orientations and five base plate materials.
